ctx.x: There was an English orchestra under the leadership of a trumpet player named Ken Coller and his brother Bill, who was playing at a club near the Ripperbahn. My band and Ken's were engaged to do a radio show which also included an Austrian tenor sax player named Hans Kohler, who was very popular in Germany. Ken played the real old time New Orleans jazz and most of the numbers he played on the show were things that I had never heard played by some of the New Orleans orchestras back home. I remember that they were…

Hans had his trio and his style was a little like Lester Young and Stan Getz. For a musical variety show, this set up was alright because there was the old style New Orleans music of Ken Colyer, the more modern Middle jazz style of me and my band, and the modern style of the 1950's played by Hans Kohler.

I closed at the Faun the 30th of September and arrived in Paris the 2nd of October. I had been in touch with the trombone player Bill Tamper, whom I had toured with a few days on another occasion, and I had signed Bill for my coming tour to replace Herman Wilson who had stayed in Germany with Donald Brown.
